articleTitle: Analysis of Threshold Voltage Options on Flip-Flop SEU Performance at GF 12-nm FinFET Node
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Flip-flops using LVT/RVT/HVT options and ring-oscillators were designed and fabricated in a 12-nm FinFET node. Radiation testing results showed significant resilience to SEE and TID effects compared to planar bulk technologies.

articleTitle: Single Event Effects and Total Ionizing Dose Characterization of MNEMOSYNE STT MRAM Prototype with 1.8V SPI Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Single event effects and total ionizing dose results for the final prototype of the memory ASIC for space applications developed in the framework of the EU H2020 Mnemosyne project are presented.

articleTitle: Irradiation of Commercial Equipment for Robotic Applications in a Highly Ionizing Radiation Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Performance of commercial equipment suitable for application in high-radiation fields on robotic platforms was evaluated at various dose rates. Total Ionizing Dose (TID) for catastrophic failure was determined for some of the tested equipment.

articleTitle: Guide to the 2023 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop Record
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: The 2023 Workshop Record has been reviewed and a table prepared to facilitate the search for radiation response data by part number, type or effect.

articleTitle: Electron Transport in Solid and Shell Geometries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Adjoint Monte Carlo gives fast, accurate effects analysis for space environments using point detectors. Ray-trace approximations are also accurate in solid geometries, but 10x too high for electrons on space system shell geometries.

articleTitle: Radiation Effects Characterization of TI AFE11612-SEP High-Density General-Purpose Monitor and Control Systems (July 2024)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: AFE11612-SEP highly integrated analog monitor and control device released for space applications. It passed total Dose of 20Krads and is latch-up immune upto 48 MeV-cm2/mg at 125C. Single Event Upset cross section was 9.33E-5 cm2/Ions.

articleTitle: TID and SEE Response of the COTS LI-OV9712-USB-M8 Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Performance degradation of the LI-OV9712-USB-M8 Camera was studied using a low dose rate <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>Co chamber and 105 MeV proton beams. Results revealed the camera present high robustness against total ionizing dose, however, failed rapidly in proton irradiation.

articleTitle: Proton Testing of Texas Instruments TDA4VM SoC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Modern space missions are handling large datasets with increased autonomy and low latency. Some processors developed for ground-based edge applications could support these space mission activities, but questions arise regarding the ability of these processors to operate reliably in the radiation environment of space. This work evaluates the performance of the Texas Instruments TDA4VM heterogeneous SoC running machine learning algorithms when irradiated with high energy protons. Device performance is reported via application cross sections and survived total ionizing dose (TID).

articleTitle: TID and SEE Evaluation of the ADALM PlutoSDR Transceiver
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: TID and SEE evaluation of the PlutoSDR transceiver were performed using low dose rate <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>Co radiation and high energy protons, respectively. TID tolerance up to 50 krad was demonstrated. Only non-destructive SEFIs were observed.

articleTitle: Total Ionizing Dose and SEE Testing of the TPS7H4011-SP 14V, 12A Synchronous Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Texas Instruments tests and discusses single-event effects and total ionizing dose of the TPS7H4011-SP, a radiation-hardened, 14V, 12A synchronous buck converter optimized for use in a space environment.

articleTitle: TID Response of Commercial-of-the-Shelf Operational Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Total ionizing dose effects on various COTS operational amplifiers were studied using low dose rate <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6-</sup>CO irradiation. Total dose tolerance to 30 krad is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Single Event Upset Characterization of the Versal® XCVC1902 Dual-Core ARM® Cortex™A72 Application Processor Unit Using Proton Irradiation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Proton induced SEU cross-section of the Versal XCVC1902 dual-core ARM® Cortex™-A72 Application Processor Unit is presented. Upset rates in the space radiation environment are estimated.

articleTitle: Single Event Upset Characterization of Microsemi RISC-V Softcore Processors on Polarfire MPF300T-1FCG1152E FPGA Using Proton Irradiation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: SEU cross-sections of the Polarfire FPGA programmed with various Microsemi RISC-V Softcore processors are presented. Upset rates in the space radiation environment are estimated and found to be acceptable for low orbit missions.

articleTitle: Compendium of Single-Event Effects Test Results for Candidate Electronics at NASA Johnson Space Center from 2023
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: We present single-event effect (SEE) test results and analysis produced by NASA JSC in 2023 for candidate electronic components and devices. Test environments include heavy ions or protons, depending on the intended use case regarding mission, environment, application, and lifetime.

articleTitle: Heavy ION and Laser-Induced Single-Event Effects Test Results for a Low-Dropout Regulator and Voltage Feedback Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Heavy ion and single photon absorption laser testing results are reported for the investigation of destructive and transient single-event effects in three radiation-hard, commercial-off-the-shelf analog parts: one low-dropout regulator and two voltage feedback amplifiers.

articleTitle: Testing of Radiation Hardened Power MOSFET Fabricated at LA Semiconductor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: VPT Components successfully completed development of a family of n-channel radiation-hardened MOSFETs at LA Semiconductor, Pocatello, ID. These MOSFETs are radiation hardened to 100 krad(Si) and SEE immune to Xe (15 MeV/n beam) at full rated drain potential. While the radiation data presented here are for the RAD7130 (100V Size 3 die, similar to the 2N7481), these radiation results are applicable to a family of n-channel MOSFETs (NMOS) from 100V to 250V and from Size 1 (∽5mm2) to Size 6 (∽58mm2). TID irradiation was performed at VPT Rad and all test parameters passed TID testing to 100 krad(Si). SEE testing was performed at Texas A&M University (TAMU) using a xenon beam to 1x10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> n/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and showed very little variation in gate current.

articleTitle: Heavy-ION Radiation Effects Facility Developments at Michigan State University
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: A review of the technical developments at Michigan State University”s heavy-ion radiation effects facility is presented.

articleTitle: Radiation Evaluation of the TPS7H6003-SP Radiation-Hardness-Assured (RHA) Gallium Nitride (GaN) Field Effect Transistor (FET) Gate Driver
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Single Events Effect (SEE) characterization and total ionizing dose (TID) results for the TPS7H6003-SP 200 V half-bridge GaN gate driver are summarized, showing very robust SEE performance up to LETEFF=75 MeV.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg and excellent TID behavior.

articleTitle: Total Non-Ionizing Dose Characterization of Microchip LX7720
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: The Total Non-Ionizing Dose characterization results of Microchip Technology's Motor Driver with Four Half-Bridge Drivers, Rotation and Position Sensing IC, the LX7720, are presented.

articleTitle: TID Effects on Random Telegraph Signals in GF 12LP FinFET Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: 12LP FINFETs from GlobalFoundries are tested under 60Co <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex> -rays. Low frequency noise measurements evidence random telegraph noise at various gate voltages in both pre- and post-rad conditions, revealing pre-existing and TID-induced prominent defects.

articleTitle: LDR Testing of 2N4861 JFET and RH1009 2.5V Reference for Europa Clipper UVS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: The 2N4861 JFET and RH1009 2.5V reference intended for the Europa Clipper mission were tested under low dose rate conditions (10 mRad/s). Both devices performed within acceptable tolerances of their applications, up to 100 krad.

articleTitle: TID and SEE Response of the AD524CDZ Instrumentation Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: TID effects on AD524CDZ instrumentation amplifier were studied using low dose rate <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>Co irradiation. SEE behavior was studied using high energy protons and Two-Photon Absorption laser to identify sensitive sectors of the device.

articleTitle: TID and ELDRS Evaluation of SiGe HBTs Integrated in a 45-nm PDSOI BiCMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Total-ionizing dose (TID) response and enhanced low-dose-rate-sensitivity (ELDRS) of newly-developed silicon-germanium (SiGe) heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) integrated in a 45-nm partially depleted silicon-on-insulator (PDSOI) BiCMOS process are evaluated. The devices showed good TID tolerance when irradiated at both low and high dose rates. The SiGe HBTs experienced increased collector leakage current due to TID in the very low base-emitter voltage region, which has not been exhibited in the previous generation devices.

articleTitle: Heavy-Ion SET and SEL Response of a Wide-Band Operational Amplifier Fabricated in the Sky Water S90LN 90 nm Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Single-event latch-up (SEL) and single-event transient (SET) testing results from heavy-ion irradiation of a custom operational amplifier (OA) designed in the SkyWater S90LN process are provided. The experiments took place at the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL) 88” Cyclotron facility using the 16 MeV/amu ion cocktail. The results show that the SET cross-section of the OA is limited to 3e-6 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and the SkyWater S90LN process exhibits SEL immunity up to an LET of 82 MeV·cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg.

articleTitle: Radiation Effects Characterization of TI ADC128S102-SEP Analog to Digital Converter (ADC) (July 2024)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: ADC128S102-SEP is an 8-channel, CMOS, 12-bit analog-to-digital converter (ADC) released for space applications. It passed 30Krad total dose and is latch-up immune upto 48 MeV-cm2/mg at 125C. The SEU was characterized at 48 MeV-cm2/mg.

articleTitle: Radiation Effects Testing of the LTC3115-1 DC/DC Voltage Converter with Heavy Ions and Protons
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Observations of heavy ion and proton induced single event effects on the LTC311S-1 DC/DC converter were made. The DC/DC converter was sensitive to SEE including SET and DSEE.

articleTitle: Single Event Effects and TID Characterization of the Frontgrade Technologies UT24CP1008 CertusPro™-NX-RT FPGA for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Single Event Effects (SEE) and Total Ionizing Dose (TID) radiation characterization was performed on Frontgrade Technologies UT24CP1008 CertusPro™-NX-RT Field Programable Gate Array (FPGA). The device was immune to Single Event Latch-up (SEL), exhibited a low Single Event Upset (SEU) cross-section, and self-recovered from most Single Event Failures (SEFs) when the scrubbing option is enabled.

articleTitle: A Space Qualified High Accuracy Linear-in-dB RMS Detector with High Dynamic Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: A high accuracy linear-in-dB RMS detector with high dynamic range was designed and tested for radiation performance. It has dynamic range 32dB, frequency 0.1 to 40GHz. The radiation tests were performed to show great radiation tolerance, including TID, heavy ion, and ELDRS tests.

articleTitle: Radiation Characterization Results of AF54RHC 300 KRAD (Si) Logic Family
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: This paper details the results for TID testing up to 400 krad (Si) and SEE testing at a maximum LETEFF= 93.3 MeV.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg for Apogee Semiconductor's AF54RHC product family. These results demonstrate suitability for space applications.

articleTitle: Radiation Test Results from a Survey of Recent e.MMC Managed Flash Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Heavy ion DSEE and NDSEE and gamma-induced TID characterization results are presented for recent-generation e.MMC managed flash devices.

articleTitle: Proton and Heavy-Ion Characterizations on Microchip PolarFire® SoC FPGA Microprocessor Subsystem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: This paper presents the initial findings of heavy ion and proton effects on the PolarFire SoC RISC-V® FPGA Micro-processor Subsystem (MSS) utilizing SiFive architecture. The results indicate the feasibility of deploying the PolarFire SoC RISC-V FPGA MSS in space, demonstrating suitability for both Low Earth Orbit (LEO) and Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) applications. Better MSS radiation performance is expected in the RT (Radiation-Tolerant) PolarFire SoC FPGA.

articleTitle: SEE and Total Dose Results of the ISL71148SLHM 8-Channel High Precision 14-bit, 900ksps SAR ADC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: We report the single event performance and low dose rate TID results of the radiation-hardened ISL71148SLHM 8 channel, high precision, 14-bit, SAR analog to digital converter.

articleTitle: Combined Total Dose and Displacement Damage Testing of the ISL71831SEH 32-Channel Analog Multiplexer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: We report the results of combined displacement damage (DD) and total ionizing dose (TID) testing performed by Renesas Electronics America on the ISL71831SEH 32-channel analog multiplexer. The part is a radiation tolerant 32 channel analog multiplexer that is fabricated in an SOI process technology to provide excellent latch-up performance. Inactive channels are isolated from the active channel by high impedance which inhibits any interaction between them. The ISL71831SEH”s low switch ON resistance allows for improved signal integrity and reduced power losses. The part is designed for cold sparing, making it compatible with redundancy techniques in high reliability applications. These tests were carried out in order to determine the ISL71831SEH response to total dose and displacement damage in a combined radiation environment. As both radiation source and fixturing issues prevent simultaneous neutron and total dose irradiation in a laboratory environment, irradiations were thus performed sequentially, with the TID exposures following the DD testing.

articleTitle: Irradiation Campaign on TinyVers: A System-on-Chip for Ultra-Low Power NN Inference
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: This paper presents the irradiation campaign that was conducted on TinyVers, a System-on-Chip designed to target ultra-low power neural network inference for applications running at the extreme edge. In order to assess its applicability in space, heavy-ion SEE and TID tests were conducted with a focus on the memories of the chip. The saturating cross-section of SRAM was in-line with literature at 3.4.10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−10</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/bit, while for eMRAM no upsets were measured. Hereby showing its potential as technology for non-volatile memory in radiation environments. Concerning TID, SRAM/eMRAM on 22nm FD-SOI is shown to be robust against TID of at least 1 kGy.

articleTitle: Understanding Commercial Power MOSFET Survivability in a Heavy-Ion Environment Using High Throughput Screening
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: We present an approach using large scale testing campaigns to select commercial-off-the-shelf components for space applications. We tested three samples each of 533 Power MOSFET part numbers, analyzing their single-event performance. This study reports the results and introduces a statistical model that uses datasheet parameters to predict device performance. Part selection and derating guidelines are proposed. The key contribution of this work is demonstrating the benefits of performing the testing at scale.

articleTitle: Total Dose and Single-Event Effects Testing of the ISL73006SLH and ISL73007SEH Point-of-Load Regulators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: We report the single event effects and total ionizing dose test results for the ISL73006SLH and ISL73007SEH radiation hardened 1 A and 3 A point-of-load regulators.

articleTitle: SEU and SEFI Characterization of a Frontgrade 18GB DDR4 Memory for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Single Event Upset (SEU) and Single Event Functional Interrupt (SEFI) radiation characterization was performed on a Frontgrade quantified, commercial off-the-shelf (QCOTS) 18GB DDR4 memory. The device was shown to be suitable for space applications.

articleTitle: Single Event Upset Characterization of the LS1046A Microprocessor Using Proton Irradiation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Experimental single event upset characterization of the LS1046A microprocessor using proton irradiation is presented. Results for various cache memory configurations, running an operating system, bare-metal, floating point and fixed point algorithms are compared.

articleTitle: New Fusion Linear Accelerator for Radiation Effects (FLARE™) Testing Facility Proof of Concept Tests and Potential Use Cases
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: SHINE Technologies has conducted two radiation effects tests with customers to demonstrate functionality and collect data at its new 14 MeV fusion neutron radiation testing facility, FLARE. Planned facility upgrades will increase user and test throughput.

articleTitle: Heavy Ion Characterization of GaN HEMT Hybrids under RF Loading
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: A pair of JHU / APL designed power amplifier hybrids using Qorvo (Triquint) GaN HEMT transistors were subjected to Heavy Ion Single Event Effects testing under application specific bias and RF loading.

Author Keywords: Single Event Burnout (SEB) Single Event Effects (SEE)

articleTitle: Assessing the Suitability of a 28nm European FPGA for CERN LHC Environments: An In-depth Radiation Qualification Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: This study conducts a comprehensive radiation qualification of the 28nm European FPGA, GateMate from Cologne Chip, focusing on its response to Single-Event Effects (SEEs) and Total Ionizing Dose (TID). The tests addressed the sensitivity of the different individual elements (SRAMs, FFs, LUTs, etc..) and evaluated the overall sensitivity of the FPGA using test circuits from the ITC99 Benchmark suite. The results of all tests are analyzed and compared with devices previously tested at CERN.

articleTitle: Radiation Evaluation of the TPS7H2140-SEP 32V, 160mΩ Quad-Channel eFuse
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Single Events Effect (SEE) characterization and Total Ionizing Dose (TID) results for the TPS7H2140-SEP 32V, 160mΩ Quad-Channel eFuse is summarized, showing very robust SEE performance up to LETEFF=48 MeV-cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg.

articleTitle: Functional Failure and Parametric Degradation of Commercial-off-the-Shelf Electronics Irradiated with High Energy Protons
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Commercial-off-the-shelf electronic components were subjected to 105 MeV proton irradiation to characterize their susceptibility to total ionizing dose and displacement damage dose.

articleTitle: Single Event Effects Testing for Integrated GaN Power Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: GaN FETs can provide higher switching rates which can lead to smaller, lighter, faster and more responsive circuits; however, historically, GaN FETs have been considered too difficult to drive and many GaN parts have shown lower reliability compared to Si FETs. This has resulted in a limited number of GaN devices thoroughly tested for use in space environments. These drawbacks have meant that, when designing for space applications, most engineers have relied on MOSFETs. Two recent innovations have caused GaN FETs to be more attractive to designers: 1) process improvements that have increased reliability and 2) driver and FET integration that has reduced design complexities. With the reliability and design complexity concerns addressed, it has become pertinent to give GaN technology a closer look. To find out if a shift towards GaN technology is feasible for space applications, Single Event Effects Testing can give insight into how these devices will perform in higher radiation environments. To this end, four CoTS parts were taken to the 88-Inch Cyclotron at Lawrence Berkely National Laboratory in July 2023 and tested for their susceptibility to single event gate rupture, latch-up and burnout. The data from testing is presented and analysis of data is given. Recommendations for further testing of similar integrated devices are provided.

articleTitle: Total Ionizing Dose Testing of a Current Sense Amplifier for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: The work presented in this paper shows the results of the Total Ionizing Dose (TID) test on current sense amplifiers of the series INA240A4-Q1. Biased and unbiased samples were characterized up to 200 krad.

articleTitle: Compendium of NASA Goddard Space Flight Center's Recent Radiation Effects Test Results
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: We present results and analysis investigating the effects of radiation on a variety of candidate spacecraft electronics to heavy ion and proton induced single-event effects (SEE), proton-induced displacement damage dose (DDD), and total ionizing dose (TID).

articleTitle: 2024 Compendium of Radiation-Induced Effects for Candidate Particle Accelerator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: The sensitivity of a variety of components for particle accelerator electronics has been analyzed against Single Event Effects, Total Ionizing Dose and Displacement Damage. The tested parts include analog, linear, digital, and mixed devices.

articleTitle: High Energy, Heavy ION Testing at Brookhaven National Laboratory: Facility & Operations Update
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: The Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider complex at BNL is the only heavy ion synchrotron facility in North America and provides high energy SEE testing capability to a large, international community. Updates on NSRL practices and plans for a new beam line dedicated to electronics testing are discussed.

articleTitle: IRRAD/CHARM, a CERN Irradiation Facility for Accelerator and Experiments Radiation Hardness Qualification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: Radiation hardness testing and qualification of ever-changing detectors, electronics components and materials is an everyday challenge. The IRRAD/CHARM facility at the CERN PS East Area has a key role in performing irradiation tests for a wide range of applications and an increasing user community.

articleTitle: Protons Evaluation of 7nm Versal™ AI Engine (AIE) Based Radiation Tolerant Platform for Deep Learning Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: This paper presents the SEE evaluation of a platform and design approach for enabling radiation-tolerant deep learning acceleration, based on the 7nm Versal™ VC1902 AI Engine (AIE), for aerospace and space 2.0 proton environments. The presented platform is suitable for deep neural network (DNN) implementations emphasizing image classification and uses 396 AIE cores. It includes solutions to mitigate both radiation-induced Single Event Functional Interrupts (SEFIs) and network datapath corruptions. The radiation-tolerant deep learning platform combines AMD's AI engine (AIE), Deep Learning Processing Unit (DPU) IP, and AMD Soft Error Mitigation (XiISEM) to mitigate SEFIs. Furthermore, a technique known as Fault Aware Training (FAT) was applied to mitigate single-event effects (SEE) in the datapath effectively. Test results from a 64MeV proton beam experiment using the ResNet-50 Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for image classification are presented. The Single Event Upset (SEU) rate, system-level SEFI rate, and neural network classification/datapath performance are compared between the standard non-mitigated and radiation-tolerant platforms. Compared to standard non-mitigated training techniques, the radiation-tolerant platform using fault-aware training methods dramatically improves overall system response. SEFI error rates are ~1.4 x 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> p/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at > 60 MeV and twice a year at 500km in LEO orbit. Datapath events are reduced by ~4X and events classification accuracy degradation > 5% are completely mitigated.

articleTitle: Results of Single Event Effect Testing at the New HEARTS@CERN High-Energy Heavy Ion Facility at CERN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Radiation Effects Data Workshop (REDW) (in conjunction with 2024 NSREC)
abstract: We present results for SEU, SEL and SEB testing of several electronic devices under high-energy heavy ion irradiation at the new HEARTS@CERN facility at CERN.
